# **Strategic Research Report: Sovereign On-Premise Agentic AI Workbench for Confidential Industrial Operations (SIH Problem ID: SIH26117)**

## **Problem Statement Dossier and Contextual Baseline**

The expansion of artificial intelligence into critical process industries has encountered a fundamental barrier: public cloud foundation models cannot comply with the strict data protection and operational confidentiality requirements governing strategic infrastructure1. In public sector undertakings (PSUs), defense manufacturing units, intelligence-linked research facilities, and continuous-process hydrocarbon refining complexes such as Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited (MRPL), daily technical workflows generate high volumes of classified operational knowledge1.  
Smart India Hackathon (SIH) 2026 Problem Statement SIH26117 formally defines the operational friction that emerges from the intersection of air-gapped data confidentiality policies and the productivity imperatives of modern enterprise workforces1.

The authentic operational and technical challenge published under SIH26117 encompasses the following structural background, problem description, and required parameters:  
Refineries, PSUs, defense-linked manufacturing facilities, and government administrative departments process routine yet highly classified technical and organizational intelligence1. Daily responsibilities involve drafting administrative approval notes, synthesizing board review presentations, verifying complex engineering calculations, authoring internal automation scripts, and auditing scanned non-destructive testing (NDT) reports and technical schematics1.  
None of this operational data can be exposed to public or commercial cloud-based AI services, such as Claude, Codex, or ChatGPT, because the underlying files contain critical infrastructure assets1. These assets include Piping & Instrumentation Diagrams (P\&IDs), proprietary crude assay valuations, financial balance sheets, commercial vendor bidding evaluations, unreleased plant designs, internal board correspondence, and long-term operating strategies1.  
Corporate policies mandate that all proprietary data remain entirely on-premises1. As a consequence, technical personnel are forced into a difficult compromise: they either perform labor-intensive analytical tasks manually—severely throttling operational throughput—or covertly upload confidential technical fragments into public web assistants1.  
While state-of-the-art open-weight reasoning and multimodal models have reached quality levels comparable to frontier cloud-hosted architectures, industrial facilities lack a unified, deployable workbench that technical personnel can operate with the same ease as commercial cloud tools1.  
The core objective is the delivery of a self-hosted, air-gapped AI workbench operating on an enterprise's internal GPU infrastructure, guaranteeing zero outbound external transmission1. The platform architecture must remain strictly model-agnostic, concurrently managing a diverse portfolio of open-weight foundation models while executing automated dynamic routing based on real-time task categorization1. Technical coding scripts, for example, require routing to models optimized for code compilation and execution, distinct from models dedicated to dense document summarization or visual parsing1. Furthermore, the system must incorporate an extensible modular design that permits hot-swapping or onboarding newly published open-weight models without rearchitecting core infrastructure1.  
The workbench must operate beyond single-turn transactional chat paradigms by functioning as an autonomous multi-step agent1. It must decompose high-level instructions into multi-phase workflows, invoke local utility tools—including secure file input/output, isolated sandbox code execution, dynamic spreadsheet computation, and local knowledge base retrieval—and iteratively refine outputs across multi-step execution loops1.  
The system must ingest heterogeneous multimodal formats, including degraded multi-page scanned PDFs, handwritten maintenance logs, technical photographs, and engineering drawings, using localized optical character recognition and vision-language backends1.  
Outputs cannot remain limited to conversational interface text; they must materialize as production-ready enterprise deliverables, such as formatted administrative approval notes, styled presentation slides, complete spreadsheets containing computational formulas, verified script code, and documented engineering calculations with explicit derivation steps1. The workbench must ground all outputs within the organization's internal technical manuals, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and historical correspondence through an air-gapped knowledge connector1.  
Technical evaluation requires an operational, localized demonstrator running on mid-range GPU hardware, highlighting dynamic model selection across distinct task categories, an end-to-end agentic workflow generating an external document deliverable from unstructured inputs, an isolated and verified sandbox execution environment, and robust multimodal technical extraction1. The platform's sovereign status must be backed by empirical evidence: verifiable system logs or active network monitoring confirming that no external HTTP handshakes, socket connections, or API telemetry occur during system operation1.

## **Industrial Threat Landscape and Data Sovereignty Mandates**

In continuous-process energy facilities, downstream crude refining, and chemical processing complexes, informational security is directly tied to physical plant safety and national energy independence2. The operational topology of public sector undertakings such as MRPL falls under rigorous oversight from the National Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Centre (NCIIPC), the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), and statutory guidelines issued by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MoPNG) and the Oil Industry Safety Directorate (OISD)22.  
The friction between strict regulatory protocols and modern productivity expectations fosters the shadow AI dilemma1. Knowledge workers in process engineering, maintenance, and administrative departments face significant operational backlogs when compiling turnaround inspection logs, assessing wall-thinning corrosion rates, drafting capital expenditure justification notes, and developing DCS automation scripts1.  
Because commercial cloud LLMs accelerate these tasks, employees are frequently tempted to bypass organizational security policies by transmitting isolated data segments through consumer endpoints1. This covert usage creates continuous exposure channels across critical industrial layers1.

| Critical Industrial Asset Class | Operational Function in Refining | Threat Consequence of Cloud Ingestion |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Piping & Instrumentation Diagrams (P\&IDs)** | Definitive mechanical and instrument schematics defining piping classes, relief valve ratings, and shutdown interlocks13. | Exposure of physical plant layouts, critical vulnerability choke points, and emergency relief configurations to foreign intelligence or adversarial entities. |
| **Crude Assay Valuations & LP Blends** | Linear programming models calculating crude slate compositions, distillation cut points, and gross refining margins (GRMs)2. | Loss of strategic commercial advantage in global crude purchasing auctions, revealing confidential pricing tolerances and yield economics2. |
| **Turnaround & Shutdown Schedules** | Integrated critical-path schedules detailing equipment decoking, catalyst replacement, and plant overhauls2. | Regional supply vulnerability leaks, market fuel distribution exposure, and timing intelligence that could be exploited to disrupt energy logistics2. |
| **Commercial Vendor Tenders & Bids** | Statutory tender documents, proprietary EPC bidding evaluations, and operational maintenance contracts1. | Severe compromise of statutory procurement integrity, violation of central vigilance regulations, and commercial litigation risks1. |
| **Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) Logs** | Ultrasonic thickness measurements, radiographic weld inspections, and high-temperature corrosion rate logs1. | Concealed structural vulnerabilities and failure probabilities can be weaponized to predict physical plant disruptions. |

The regulatory environment within India's public sector imposes legal sanctions for data sovereignty violations2. The Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA), alongside NCIIPC mandates for critical national infrastructure, establishes that proprietary plant architectures, commercial supply commitments, and engineering schematics must reside within sovereign domestic control22.  
Furthermore, OISD standards mandate that process control networks (Level 3 and Level 4 of the industrial Purdue Model) maintain deterministic logical separation from outside networks through Demilitarized Zones (DMZs) and physical air gaps22. Consequently, an enterprise AI assistant can only achieve production clearance if it proves absolute, host-level network containment, ensuring that no internal network socket initiates wide-area transmission1.

## **Technical Deep Dive: Open-Weight Model Ecosystem on Mid-Range Hardware**

A key engineering requirement of SIH26117 is demonstrating full operational capability on mid-range GPU hardware, specifically within a 24GB to 48GB VRAM envelope1. This requirement ensures the workbench can be deployed on departmental servers or engineering workstations (such as an NVIDIA RTX 3090, RTX 4090, or professional RTX A4000/A5000/A6000) without requiring multi-node data center infrastructure10.  
Executing multi-modal vision tasks, complex engineering reasoning, and code compilation on a single mid-range accelerator requires careful management of model parameter scales, quantization strategies, and Key-Value (KV) cache memory9. High-throughput inference runtimes, such as vLLM, utilize PagedAttention algorithms to prevent memory fragmentation and support concurrent serving within constrained VRAM limits9.

| Open-Weight Model Engine | Parameter Scale & Quantization Profile | Specialized Functional Assignment | Memory Consumption (VRAM Footprint) | Execution Capabilities & Behavioral Limits |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B** | 14 Billion Parameters (AWQ / FP8 / Int4)10 | Deep Engineering Calculations & Formal Approval Memos1 | 10 GB – 14 GB10 | Employs reinforced Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning for mathematical modeling; fits alongside an auxiliary model in 24GB10. |
| **DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B** | 8 Billion Parameters (GGUF Q4\_K\_M / Int8)38 | Rapid Workflow Planning, Task Decomposition, Model Routing14 | 6 GB – 8 GB38 | Low inference latency and small memory footprint; ideal for iterative agent planning, routing, and reflection loops15. |
| **Qwen2.5-Coder-7B / 14B-Instruct** | 7B / 14B Parameters (AWQ / FP8)38 | Automation Scripting, Data Parsing, Sandboxed Tool Execution1 | 6 GB – 12 GB10 | Matches top closed models on HumanEval; produces verified Python, shell, and SQL pipelines for execution sandboxes17. |
| **Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct** | 7 Billion Parameters (Native FP16 / AWQ)10 | Scanned Document OCR, Field Photos, Visual QA1 | 8 GB – 14 GB10 | Dynamic resolution vision-language backbone; parses technical layouts and handwritten maintenance logs without downscaling1. |
| **ColPali (PaliGemma-based)** | \~3 Billion Parameters (Native / Int8)18 | Multi-Vector Visual Retrieval for Drawings and Dense Tables18 | 4 GB – 6 GB18 | Direct visual token indexing; bypasses OCR errors by embedding document page images into multi-vector spaces18. |
| **DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B** | 32 Billion Parameters (AWQ / Int4)10 | Complex Plant Root-Cause and Thermodynamic Analysis1 | 20 GB – 24 GB10 | Strong analytical reasoning matching frontier models; utilizes nearly all available memory on a 24GB card10. |

Operating within a 24GB VRAM capacity requires careful memory allocation strategies9. If an architecture concurrently loads a vision model (Qwen2.5-VL-7B at \~10GB), a coding engine (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B at \~6GB), and a general planning agent (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-8B at \~6GB), static parameter storage reaches \~22GB, leaving minimal memory for dynamic KV caches during multi-turn sessions10.  
To address these hardware boundaries, enterprise architectures utilize two primary orchestration strategies:

* Quantized Colocation: Models are converted to 4-bit or 8-bit weight profiles (via AWQ or GPTQ) combined with FP8 KV caches, enabling multiple compact models to sit concurrently in GPU memory for low-latency dispatch10.  
* Serial Offloading via High-Speed System RAM: A lightweight orchestration router resides permanently in VRAM, while larger specialized models (such as 14B reasoning or coding engines) are loaded and unloaded dynamically through PCIe Gen4/Gen5 lanes using unified serving platforms like llama.cpp or vLLM9.

When deployed on a 48GB GPU platform, such as an NVIDIA RTX A6000 or a dual RTX 4090 installation, memory constraints ease substantially, allowing 32B reasoning models and vision-language engines to operate concurrently without dynamic swapping11.

## **Advanced R\&D: Dynamic Model Routing and Multi-Model Orchestration**

A critical bottleneck in early enterprise LLM deployments is the tendency to route all tasks to a single foundation model regardless of prompt complexity or modality requirements1. The problem statement mandates that the workbench avoid vendor or model lock-in, dynamically routing tasks across specialized open-weight models based on operational context1.  
Modern research in model routing emphasizes sub-50ms dispatch mechanisms that direct queries without incurring high computational overhead14.

### **Routing Paradigms: RouteLLM vs. System-Level Semantic Routers**

Model dispatch architectures generally follow two primary technical patterns: preference-trained regression classifiers and vector-based semantic gating14.  
Preference-Trained Classifiers (such as RouteLLM, developed by Berkeley LMSYS) utilize empirical win-probability scoring derived from human evaluations and benchmark data14. The router estimates the probability ![][image1] that a larger, computationally demanding model will provide a meaningfully better output than a lightweight model14. RouteLLM supports several underlying routing strategies:

* Matrix Factorization: Queries and model embeddings are mapped into a shared latent space where inner products predict performance14.  
* BERT/DeBERTa Intent Classifiers: Small encoder models trained to categorize query complexity and domain requirements directly14.  
* Similarity-Weighted Ranking: Queries are matched against anchor benchmark examples to calculate weighted Elo ratings14.  
* Causal Small LLM Classifiers: Dedicated 1B–3B parameter language models generate structured JSON routing instructions14.

System-Level Semantic Routers (such as the vLLM Semantic Router) operate by clustering vector embeddings14. User queries are converted into dense vector representations and matched via cosine similarity against curated subspaces that represent distinct operational domains—such as mathematical engineering, automated coding, visual schematic parsing, and internal document search14. Semantic routers can also integrate safety screening and hallucination detection (such as HaluGate) to assess context sufficiency prior to generation15.

### **Mechanistic Routing and Mathematical Signal Formulation**

Recent research in mechanistic routing demonstrates that simple lexical or semantic features often fail to detect task difficulty or model-specific failure modes43. Instead of relying solely on surface embeddings, advanced routers evaluate internal activations extracted during the early prefill stages of small open-weight encoder models43.  
A reliable routing signal requires three structural conditions in the representation space: high effective dimensionality, high isotropy, and clear linear separability between solvable and failure-prone tasks43.  
The effective dimensionality (![][image2]) of the representation space is derived from the participation ratio of the covariance matrix eigenvalues (![][image3]) of the activation vectors43:  
![][image4]  
A higher ![][image2] ensures that task characteristics are distributed broadly across latent dimensions rather than collapsing into low-rank representations43.  
Representational anisotropy (![][image5]) measures the directional uniformity of the embedding vectors (![][image6]) and is expressed as43:  
![][image7]  
Lower anisotropy prevents the "narrow cone" problem where outlier dimensions dominate the latent space, preserving clear geometric separation between different technical domains43.  
Linear separation between reasoning-intensive tasks (![][image8]) and routine administrative requests (![][image9]) is evaluated using the Fisher Separability Criterion (![][image10])43:  
![][image11]  
By maximizing ![][image10], the routing engine dispatches complex thermodynamic balance calculations to deep reasoning models such as DeepSeek-R1-Distill-14B/32B, while directing standard document search and boilerplate memo formatting to fast 7B/8B models10.

### **Autonomous Agentic Execution Loops**

Unlike simple conversational bots, an agentic workbench operates via iterative decision cycles: planning, tool invocation, observation, and self-reflection1.  
The primary planning model decomposes high-level requests into deterministic directed acyclic graphs (DAGs)1. The agent then invokes local tools through structured JSON or Python function calls, interfacing with file systems, local vector stores, sandboxed code runners, and mathematical libraries1.  
Following tool execution, the agent evaluates standard output (stdout), standard error (stderr), or structured return objects17. If a script encounters errors or detects anomalous calculation results, the agent adjusts parameters and re-executes the tool instead of terminating or outputting an unverified answer1. Once intermediate calculations and document extractions are verified, the agent passes compiled data structures to programmatic generation engines to produce formatted enterprise files (.docx, .pptx, .xlsx)1.

## **Multimodal Ingestion of Complex Industrial Artifacts (P\&IDs and Technical Documentation)**

A critical requirement of SIH26117 is processing multimodal documentation, including scanned inspection logs, handwritten maintenance records, and Piping & Instrumentation Diagrams (P\&IDs)1. In refining and chemical manufacturing, P\&IDs serve as the core visual representation of plant operational topology25. However, these engineering drawings present significant challenges for standard vision-language models12.

### **Structural Anatomy of Piping and Instrumentation Diagrams**

A P\&ID is not an artistic illustration; it is a dense schematic governed by strict engineering standards such as ISA 5.1 and ISO 1461713. The drawing integrates four distinct layers of operational data:

* Equipment Layer: Depicts major physical process units—such as distillation towers, heat exchangers, reactors, and pumps—labeled with standardized plant equipment tags (e.g., 11-C-101, P-204A/B)25.  
* Piping Layer: Illustrates process fluid lines, detailing nominal pipe sizes, piping material specifications (PMS), fluid service codes, insulation types, and flow direction arrows25.  
* Instrumentation Layer: Uses standardized circular bubbles containing functional identifiers (e.g., FT for Flow Transmitter, PIC for Pressure Indicator Controller) and loop numbers25. Specific line patterns denote signal types, such as pneumatic lines, electronic 4-20mA loops, software interlocks, or capillary tubing25.  
* Control Logic & Safety Layer: Details safety relief valves (PSVs), emergency shutdown (ESD) interlocks, and control relationships connecting sensors to actuators and valves25.

### **Failure Modes of Conventional OCR and Standard VLMs**

When processing P\&IDs and scanned engineering documents, off-the-shelf multimodal models encounter several technical failure modes12:

* Micro-Resolution Data Loss: Engineering drawings are drafted on large paper formats (ISO A0, A1, or ANSI D/E)12. Standard vision-language models downscale input images to fixed patch grids (such as ![][image12] or ![][image13] pixels), which blurs small alphanumeric text inside instrument bubbles, distorts flow direction arrows, and breaks thin schematic lines12.  
* Disruption of Topological Continuity: Standard attention mechanisms operate across image patches independently, making them incapable of tracing continuous piping paths across dense, intersecting lines12.  
* Non-Standard Symbology: Although ISA standards provide common baselines, operating refineries often accumulate proprietary symbology variations ("house styles") across plant expansion phases, causing standard recognition models to fail25.

| Technical Document Processing Layer | Conventional Pipeline Bottlenecks | Advanced Computer Vision & VLM Approaches |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **High-Resolution Text & Tag Parsing** | Standard OCR engines fail on text rotated at ![][image14] or embedded within complex drawing geometries46. | Deep learning text detection (such as CRAFT or PaddleOCR) using high-resolution sliding-window patch extraction19. |
| **Symbol Detection (Valves, Pumps, Bubbles)** | Generic object detectors miss small, densely packed, visually similar symbols12. | Fine-tuned YOLO architectures (YOLOv8/v10), Relationformer models, or One-Shot Dynamic Graph CNNs (OSSR-PID)12. |
| **Connectivity & Line Tracing** | Standard Hough transforms break at intersections, elbows, and symbol borders12. | Morphological path tracing, skeletonization algorithms, and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) generating Labeled Property Graphs (LPGs)12. |
| **Schematic Page Retrieval** | Traditional text chunking loses all spatial and graphical context present in schematics and tables18. | Vision-language late-interaction multi-vector retrieval via ColPali, indexing visual token patches directly without preliminary OCR stripping18. |

### **Advanced Visual Document Retrieval: The ColPali Framework**

To avoid the data loss caused by text-only chunking, modern multimodal RAG pipelines utilize visual retrieval architectures like ColPali18.  
Built on vision-language foundation backends (such as PaliGemma), ColPali processes entire document pages as images, generating late-interaction multi-vector representations for every visual patch on the page18. When an engineer submits a query regarding a specific pump bypass or instrument loop, ColPali matches query tokens directly against the visual patch embeddings of the original drawing18.  
This preserves document geometry and spatial relationships, enabling accurate retrieval of complex P\&ID schematics, dense inspection tables, and handwritten signatures without relying on brittle OCR extraction18.

## **Air-Gapped Code Execution and Sandboxing Security**

A central capability of an agentic workbench is programmatic synthesis: translating user instructions into Python, shell, or SQL scripts to perform mathematical modeling, data extraction, and document generation1.  
However, allowing an autonomous AI model to execute arbitrary code within a critical industrial infrastructure environment introduces major security risks17.

### **Threat Modeling for Local Agentic Code Execution**

Deploying an autonomous code execution engine on internal servers creates several distinct threat vectors17:

* Indirect Prompt Injection: Ingested documents (such as vendor technical bids or scanned PDFs containing adversarial prompts) can instruct the LLM to execute malicious system commands, alter local configurations, or attempt host compromise17.  
* Host Kernel Exploitation: Untrusted code can exploit vulnerabilities in shared Linux kernels (such as container escape CVE-2025-59528) to break out of container boundaries and compromise host systems and GPU drivers17.  
* Resource Exhaustion: Scripts containing runaway recursive functions, fork bombs, or uncontrolled memory allocations can exhaust compute and memory resources, causing system instability17.  
* Network Scanning and Lateral Movement: Generated scripts might attempt to open network sockets, scan internal IP ranges within refinery operational networks (Purdue Level 3/Level 4), or initiate outbound connections17.

### **Comparative Isolation Runtimes: Docker vs. gVisor vs. MicroVMs**

Protecting host systems from untrusted agent-generated code requires decoupling execution environments from the host kernel17. Standard Docker containers share the host Linux kernel through namespaces and cgroups, which does not provide an adequate security boundary for untrusted code execution17. Modern architectures use hardened virtualization technologies to enforce strong process isolation17.

| Security & Runtime Parameter | Standard Docker Containers | Hardened Containers (gVisor / runsc) | Hardware MicroVMs (AWS Firecracker / CubeVM) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Isolation Architecture** | Shared host Linux kernel; isolated via standard namespaces and cgroups17. | User-space application kernel (Sentry) that intercepts and virtualizes system calls17. | Hardware-assisted virtualization (KVM); boots an isolated minimal guest kernel per instance17. |
| **Initialization Latency** | 50ms – 200ms17 | 100ms – 300ms (sub-second execution startup)17 | 60ms – 150ms (optimized minimal VMM boot paths)17 |
| **System Call Overhead** | \< 1% native execution speed17 | 10% – 20% overhead on high-frequency system calls17 | 15% – 30% overhead; hardware-accelerated memory virtualization17 |
| **Host Kernel Attack Surface** | Broad; direct exposure of host kernel system call tables17. | Minimized; \~70% of system calls handled safely within user-space Go17. | Negligible; host kernel isolated behind hardware KVM virtualization boundaries17. |
| **Suitability for SIH26117** | Insufficient for untrusted execution in critical PSUs17. | Optimal balance of security isolation, low latency, and OCI image compatibility17. | Maximum security; ideal for multi-tenant setups, though requires virtualization support17. |

For an on-premise industrial workbench running on a single workstation or edge server, Google's gVisor (runsc) provides an effective balance of security and efficiency17. Because it integrates as a drop-in OCI runtime replacement for Docker, it allows Python scripts that parse spreadsheets or calculate corrosion rates to run inside a virtualized user-space kernel without overhead-heavy VM orchestration17.

### **Zero-Trust Network Isolation and Verification**

To satisfy the sovereign air-gap mandate of SIH26117, sandboxed environments and host services must enforce complete network isolation1:

* Network Namespacing: Code execution sandboxes run with network access completely disabled (--network none or isolated loopback-only interfaces)17.  
* Kernel-Level Socket Monitoring: Host systems use extended Berkeley Packet Filters (eBPF) to trace network-related system calls (tcp\_v4\_connect, udp\_sendmsg), providing verifiable proof that no process attempts outbound connections17.  
* Ephemeral File Systems: Sandbox containers mount root filesystems as read-only, using temporary, size-restricted in-memory volumes (tmpfs) for file generation that are securely wiped upon process termination17.

## **Enterprise Grounding, Verification, and Deliverable Generation**

Industrial users require concrete business deliverables rather than conversational chat responses1. When a maintenance engineer uploads an ultrasonic inspection log, the required outcome is an administrative approval note formatted to PSU standards, an Excel sheet calculating corrosion rates and retirement dates, or a presentation deck for an operations review meeting1.

### **Grounded Retrieval-Augmented Generation Architecture**

To eliminate hallucinations in mission-critical engineering workflows, the workbench must ground model outputs in verified plant documentation via an air-gapped RAG pipeline1:

* Hybrid Sparse and Dense Retrieval: Combines keyword search (BM25) for locating exact equipment tag numbers and technical standard codes with dense vector embeddings (such as BGE or E5) for conceptual search9.  
* Visual Layout Ingestion: Employs visual retrieval models (ColPali) to preserve multi-column tables, technical drawing symbols, and spatial document structures without text-stripping errors18.  
* Cross-Encoder Reranking: Uses lightweight local rerankers (such as BGE-Reranker-Large) to score and filter retrieved contexts, ensuring that only the most relevant operational data enters the model's context window50.

### **Deterministic Office Deliverable Compilation Pipeline**

Generating compliant enterprise documents requires decoupling analytical reasoning from file generation16. Large language models often produce corrupt styling or malformed binary structures when attempting to generate complex document formats directly14.  
To ensure consistent document quality, the system uses a two-stage compilation pipeline:  
In the first stage, the reasoning model evaluates engineering data, regulatory thresholds, and equipment logs, producing a structured JSON payload validated against strict Pydantic schemas16.  
In the second stage, an isolated sandbox environment ingests this validated JSON data and populates pre-approved corporate templates using deterministic Python libraries16.  
The compilation process is distributed across specialized document tools:

* Microsoft Word (.docx): Handled by python-docx to generate formal administrative approval notes, applying standard typography, departmental headers, reference codes, and signature blocks1.  
* Microsoft Excel (.xlsx): Handled by openpyxl to build structured spreadsheets containing raw data, computational formulas, standard deviation metrics, and conditional formatting rules1.  
* Microsoft PowerPoint (.pptx): Handled by python-pptx to assemble executive presentations, embedding inspection images, technical charts, and structured summaries into corporate slide layouts1.

By separating logical reasoning from document compilation, the workbench ensures that output files are structurally valid, properly styled, and immediately suitable for operational use1.

## **Hackathon Evaluation Parameters and Empirical Validation Protocols**

The evaluation parameters for SIH26117 establish clear technical criteria to separate functional, production-ready platforms from basic, cloud-dependent prototypes1. Evaluators and hackathon juries assess entries across five core pillars1:

| Evaluation Dimension | Core Technical Verification Method | Critical Disqualifying Factors |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Proof of Sovereign Air-Gap** | Live host-level network inspection (using tcpdump, Wireshark, or eBPF tracing) verifying zero outbound DNS resolutions, HTTP requests, or external socket handshakes during all operations1. | Any outbound background network calls (such as model registry updates, telemetry pings, remote font requests, or cloud API fallbacks)1. |
| **Automated Dynamic Model Routing** | Automated classification and dispatch of heterogeneous tasks across at least two distinct open-weight models without manual operator intervention (e.g., code tasks to Qwen2.5-Coder; document tasks to Qwen2.5-VL/DeepSeek-R1)1. | Hardcoded, static single-model processing; manual UI dropdowns requiring users to select backend models manually1. |
| **End-to-End Agentic Task Execution** | Autonomous multi-step execution from raw input to finished deliverable: parsing a scanned inspection log, calculating corrosion thinning, verifying thresholds, and compiling a formatted Word/Excel document in a sandbox1. | Simple chat-based text responses; single-turn conversational output without intermediate tool execution or file system artifact generation1. |
| **Hardware Bounding & Memory Efficiency** | Stable performance on mid-range GPU hardware (![][image15] 24GB to 48GB VRAM) using advanced quantization and memory management without Out-Of-Memory (OOM) failures under load1. | Hardware requirements that exceed accessible mid-range bounds; system crashes or process kills during concurrent model invocations1. |
| **Multimodal Extraction Quality** | Accurate parsing of complex visual documents, including degraded multi-page scans, handwritten logs, and high-resolution engineering drawings (P\&IDs)1. | Extensive OCR hallucinations; inability to extract structured tabular data or recognize standardized engineering symbols18. |

To demonstrate compliance effectively, the platform must provide comprehensive system visibility1. A verifiable entry should incorporate an integrated monitoring dashboard showing real-time VRAM allocation, GPU compute utilization, active model process identifiers, sandbox system call logs, and active network interface metrics confirming that outbound transmission remains at zero bytes1.

## **Conclusions**

The problem statement formulated by Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited under SIH26117 highlights an essential requirement for the industrial adoption of artificial intelligence in sovereign and critical infrastructure domains1. Transitioning from external, cloud-hosted AI tools to secure on-premise workbenches requires solving core systems engineering challenges: operating advanced models within the memory constraints of mid-range GPU hardware, routing tasks dynamically across specialized open-weight models, and maintaining zero-trust sandboxed environments that protect vital IT and OT networks1.  
An analysis of existing market offerings indicates that while individual technologies exist—such as vLLM inference runtimes, RouteLLM classification engines, gVisor execution sandboxes, and ColPali visual retrieval models—off-the-shelf platforms remain either cloud-dependent or architecturally rigid14.  
Meeting the requirements of SIH26117 requires an integrated agentic architecture where sovereign air-gapped operation serves as the primary design foundation1. By combining autonomous agent workflows with verifiable local sandboxing, specialized open-weight foundation models, and deterministic office deliverable generation, organizations across refining, defense manufacturing, and public administration can unlock substantial productivity gains while maintaining absolute data sovereignty1.
